correctness.rationale: For any 0/1 subset of Z8×Z2, the sum of eighth roots of unity vanishes exactly when the four cyclotomic count pairs are equal, since Phi8=X^4+1. Thus spectrum iff D(B) is a subset of Fourier zeros Z(A) at equal cardinality, and tiling iff disjoint nonzero differences and cardinality product 16. Computing exact difference masks for each of 65535 nonempty subsets, their 15-bit histograms and subset zeta transforms proves all s(A) and t(A) counts including vanishing for non-divisor sizes. Complete partition by 16 automorphisms times 16 translations yields precisely 43 orbits and re-sums to 1611 spectral sets. The included verifier was actually executed; brute pair tests independently reproduce every positive basis count for k=2,4,8. No floating-point error or infinite extrapolation arises.

originality.rationale: The proven new claim is quantitative: 1611 spectral subsets and their spectra and complement multiplicities in exactly 43 affine classes for the group of exponent eight. Zhang (arXiv:2109.08400, Theorem 1.5) subsumes the qualitative yes/no equivalence for the group but not this count; Malikiosis is cyclic, and the two closest public order-16 tables concern groups of exponent four. Full text of both named primary papers was examined. Specific queries for the group aliases, exact counts, and basis multiplicities returned no matching table; this supports best-knowledge originality but does not prove global novelty.
residual_risks: Unindexed earlier enumerations of Z8 × Z2, unpublished computational tables, or specialist appendices might record equivalent counts.
The two closest quantitative group-order comparisons were evaluated from indexed scientific summaries, not their complete papers.
Originality is a same-model, best-knowledge assessment, not independent priority certification.

value.rationale: A complete exact spectrum/tiling incidence classification in Z8 × Z2 naturally refines the prior yes/no Fuglede result, distinguishing 43 affine classes and giving number-of-spectrum counts for every subset. The exponent-eight group is not interchangeable with two previously tabulated exponent-four order-16 groups. New concrete phenomena include 672 eight-point sets with exactly two spectra and 6 with 256, plus reversed four-point (s,t) multiplicity pairs (16,32) and (32,16). These are structural, naturally defined finite Fourier invariants useful when comparing Fourier sampling bases and tiling complements, not arbitrary selected examples.
